candidate.answerReason: Bisecting the 120° central triangle gives an apothem equal to 6 cos 60° = 3, equivalently the short leg of a 30° right triangle.

methods.label: Cosine in a central triangle
methods.explanation: The central angle is \(120^\circ\), and the apothem is \(R\cdot\cos60^\circ=6\times1/2=3\).
methods.levelReason: Acute-angle cosine and its special-angle values are within the supplied Grade 9 curriculum.

methods.label: A 30° right triangle
methods.explanation: Let \(ABC\) be the equilateral triangle, \(O\) its circumcenter, and \(M\) the midpoint of \(AB\). In an equilateral triangle, each perpendicular bisector is also an angle bisector. Hence \(OM\perp AB\) and \(\angle OAM=30^\circ\). Thus \(AO=6\) is the hypotenuse of right triangle \(AOM\). The side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, so the apothem is \(OM=6/2=3\).
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 equilateral-triangle geometry and the 30° right-triangle property.
